question: why cmdr_recut reported RECUT_ABORT twice on this candidate, reproduced rather than relayed

merge_shape_against_tip.method: difflib.SequenceMatcher over each file's lines with a trailing CR stripped; a row that matches after stripping but not before is an ending-only rewrite, the churn a three-way merge cannot attribute to a hunk

cause: r3 rewrote rows of frontend/src/app/v8Types.ts that it never edited: that file carries 14 bare-LF rows on the line (tip: 78 CRLF and 14 bare-LF rows) while r3 shipped 102 CRLF and 0 bare-LF rows, so the merge sees ending-only churn on rows the line also touches -- the same whole-file shape the ledger records for *.py under ORD-0532 (.gitattributes at the tip: `*.py text eol=lf`)
fix_proof: r4 rebuilds that one file from the tip's own bytes and inserts only this order's hunk: against the tip r4 adds 14 rows and removes 1 (the legs row it splits) with 0 ending-only rewrites, and keeps the 14 bare-LF rows exactly as the tip has them. Measured the same way, r3 against the tip carried 16 ending-only rewrites on top of the rows this order really changes -- that surplus is what the gate read as whole-file churn.
